notes: Scan 125 has no visible author page number at the head and has pencil foliation 124 at lower left. Reader_b viewed the whole page once and each native half once, then all 8 unique first-pass crops. No OCR, external research, other page files, or TeX compilation was used.

The line_count of 20 counts 12 principal prose baselines (including the two live interlinear replacement lines and two long cancelled old lines), 3 object baselines in (197), 2 object baselines in (198), and the three displayed baselines for the inequality, (199) and (200). The four small def labels and pencil foliation are inventoried within their elements rather than counted as additional principal baselines. The short cancelled formula shares the principal level of the following a donnée clause; relatifs is displaced below/left.

S125-01. The page says that (194) yields a corresponding morphism that is épi lisse. Diagram (197) identifies its two objects with base changes of G_d and G_{d′} and corresponding lattice-tensor descriptions. The referenced (194) is not supplied on this page and was not consulted; no proof of epimorphy or smoothness was verified.

All four definition labels visibly read unaccented def. The vertical marks are pairs of straight strokes without arrowheads. The single horizontal arrow in (197) has a small full head at the right. In (198), the horizontal relation has one wave and one straight bar; a double-straight equality with an added wave would add a stroke.

S125-02. Diagram (198) presents a corresponding contracted-product isomorphism. Its written indices and definitions are retained: the left top P has a d-prime/double-prime cluster while the lower left begins P_d; the underbraced right P(d,d′)_d is defined against an expression beginning P_{d′}. This differs from the pairing suggested by the analogous G labels in (197), but the visible subscript clusters, the lower-left product sign, and the new low-G-index ambiguity are not repaired by the expected mathematics. The page's isomorphism is carried as background, not proved.

In (198), the right underbrace belongs only to the first P factor. The following wedge and G factor occupy a separate cell so that the vertical definition attaches to the underbraced factor. The group sits below the wedge. A low d-like loop between G and its parenthesis is retained through G_d|G; it is not silently erased or asserted as a definite extra index.

The two dark prime-height remnants at the end of the top indices in (197) and (198) are included in d′|d′′ uncertainties. One prime is readable at each place; the added dark ink might be a second prime or cancellation/retracing of a former sign. No definite deleted prime is invented.

The source has two live replacement lines interleaved above the separately cancelled old groupoid lines. Both are marked as insertions. The deleted paragraph is transcribed as one continuous readable deleted span, while its two physical baselines and the positions of the replacements are recorded in the inventory and checks. The later short cancelled ΠP formula is a separate deletion and retains its internal uncertainty.

After the short cancelled formula, the source reads a donnée: a single unaccented a-shaped graphic unit, a blank interval, then the initial d of donnée. Neither a separate la nor an accent on a is visible. The wording is preserved without grammatical normalization. Relatifs is live and has a long f-like descender, but its ending stays uncertain.

S125-03. A limited formal check concerns extension of structure group only. For homomorphisms G→H→K and a right G-torsor P, the map [[p,h],k]↦[p,ψ(h)k] gives (P×^G H)×^H K→P×^G K. It respects both G- and H-equivalence relations; [p,k]↦[[p,1],k] is its inverse. This checks the formal associativity underlying a possible transitivity statement. It does not verify the manuscript's specific base changes, all preceding maps, the uncertain product sign, or the index pairings in (198).

S125-04. The remaining text introduces the three local systems T(d,d′,d′′) indexed by d,d′,d′′ and corresponding tori over D(d,d′,d′′), under d≥d′≥d′′. These object names and the non-strict inequalities were read from this page. Their construction and the specific transitivity relations are carried as background without a general proof check.

In (199), the first label digit is retraced. The retained reading is 199; no separate earlier digit can be recovered securely. The first T has one upright and a following parenthesis whose top meets its bar; it is not another capital Π. The three terminal indices and the three commas in (199) are retained. Formula (200) has the three corresponding G terms without a supplied terminal point or comma.
H's editorial note about interchanged definitions is not manuscript ink and is not transcribed. Its observation is discussed only as the visible index-pairing issue above.
